CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_SSH_PORT: SSH port (default: SSH connection port, then platform port):
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL: Principal (default: connection username, in the platform's realm):
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_WINRM_CERTIFICATE: Trusted certificate (SHA-256 fingerprint, empty: the platform's CA, or else the first one seen):
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_CHECKOUT_EXCLUSIVE: Only one holder at a time:
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_REQUEST_EXEMPT: Allow access without a request (ignored when approvals are required):
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_REVEAL_PASSWORD: Let users holding access see the password:

PAM.HELP_BADGES: Counts shown next to your name and on their settings tab, so you notice what needs your attention. Turning a badge off only hides the count; the tabs still list everything.
PAM.HELP_CHECKOUTS: Passwords and connection access currently held by users. Revoking a checkout ends it immediately, closes the holder's open sessions on that connection, and rotates the password if it is managed to rotate after each use.
PAM.HELP_CONNECTIONS: Connections assigned to a platform (set up on the Platforms tab). Rotation logs in to the target with the stored credentials, changes the password as the platform describes, and stores the new password only after the target accepts it.
PAM.HELP_HOST_KEY: Key trusted for this target: recorded at the first contact, or the one that last passed the check. Rotation refuses a different key until the new one is pasted into the connection's "Trusted SSH host key" field.
PAM.HELP_PLATFORMS: Platforms describe how passwords of a group of systems are changed, and when. A connection is managed once it is assigned a platform in its "Password management" settings.
PAM.HELP_STORED_SECRETS: Passwords of this platform are stored. Leave their fields empty to keep them, unless you change where they are sent (server, port, encryption, trusted certificate or CA certificates): enter them again then.
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_CASE: Wait until the output since the last send matches the regular expression of one of the cases, run the lines of the case matching first in the output, then continue after @end. Cases cannot hold other cases
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_COMMENT: Comment, ignored, as are empty lines
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_ESCAPE: Send a line starting with @ or # as-is
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_EXPECT: Wait until the output since the last send contains this text
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_REGEX: Wait until the output since the last send matches this regular expression
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_SEND: Any other line is sent exactly as typed (spaces included), followed by Enter
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_SEND_EMPTY: Press Enter (or "@send text" to send text)
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_TIMEOUT: Seconds each following expect may wait (default 10)
PAM.HELP_TYPE_KERBEROS: MIT Kerberos, Heimdal and Active Directory domains, over kpasswd (RFC 3244). Changes principal passwords as an admin principal or as the principal itself.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_WINRM: Local Windows accounts only, over HTTPS only. Sets their passwords as an administrator or as the account itself (which must then be an administrator); for domain accounts, use LDAP or Kerberos. Host certificates are trusted on first contact, or checked against your CA's certificates.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_LDAP: OpenLDAP, Active Directory and other directories, over LDAPS or StartTLS. Changes account passwords as an administrator or as the account itself. Active Directory requires encryption.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_SSH: Any system reachable over SSH: a send/expect script changes the password, such as passwd on Linux or net user on Windows (OpenSSH). The host key is trusted on first contact, or pinned on the connection.

REQUEST.TEXT_AVAILABLE_EXCLUSIVE: The password will be checked out to you alone for {MINUTES} minutes and then released automatically.

REQUEST.TEXT_LAST_EXPIRED: Your last request expired before it was approved.
REQUEST.TEXT_NEEDS_APPROVAL: This password needs {REQUIRED, plural, one{1 approval} other{# approvals}}. Once approved, it is checked out to you for {MINUTES} minutes.

PAM_HISTORY.HELP_HISTORY: Every checkout of a password or of access to a connection, active or ended, newest first. Search matches the user, account, reason, or how and by whom a checkout ended. Click a column header to sort.

PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_HISTORY: Every decided request you may see, newest first: approved, denied, cancelled by its requester, or expired. Search matches the requester, connection, account, reason, decision, who decided, or the reason for a denial. Click a reason to read it in full, or a column header to sort.
PAM_APPROVALS.FIELD_DENY_REASON: Reason for the denial (shown to the requester):
PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_PENDING: Requests awaiting approval that you may decide on: those of the connections your approval permission (or that of one of your groups) covers. Administrators see all. A request needs as many distinct approvers as its connection requires; one denial rejects it. Once approved, the requester's checkout starts. Requests left pending for 24 hours expire.
PAM_APPROVALS.INFO_BADGE: {COUNT, plural, one{1 request awaits} other{# requests await}} your approval

PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_APPROVE_CONNECTION: May approve requests for this connection
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_APPROVE_GROUP: May approve requests for every connection in this group, including ones added later
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_SELECT_GROUP: Members may approve requests for the connections and connection groups ticked "Approve" in the connections list below ({COUNT} selected).
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_SELECT_USER: This user may approve requests for the connections and connection groups ticked "Approve" in the connections list below ({COUNT} selected).

PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.HELP_EXPORT: Download the platforms listed, without their passwords, to import them here or on another server.
PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.HELP_RESTORE_DEFAULTS: Add back the default platforms, Unix and Windows, that are missing.
PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.TEXT_CONFIRM_RESTORE: Add back the default platforms that are missing? Platforms with their names are left as they are, even if changed.
PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.TEXT_NOTHING_RESTORED: Every default platform already exists: {NAMES}. Nothing was changed.

PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.ERROR_NEWER_VERSION: This file was exported by a newer version of the extension.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.ERROR_NOT_PLATFORMS: The provided file must be a platforms export, from the Platforms tab, or a list of platforms.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.ERROR_READ: The provided file could not be read.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_EXISTING: Platforms are matched by name. One that already exists refuses the import unless "Update existing platforms" is ticked. An update cannot change a platform's type, and keeps the passwords it stores when the file leaves them out, unless a setting deciding where they are sent changes (such as its server or port): the file must then give them.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_EXISTING_PLATFORM_MODE: Update existing platforms whose names match those in the file, rather than refusing the import. Passwords left out of the file are kept.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_JSON_DESCRIPTION: A platform import file is what Export writes on the Platforms tab: an object naming its format and version, with a list of platforms. A bare list of platforms is read as well. Each platform has a name, a type (ssh, ldap, kerberos or winrm), its settings and its rotation policy, and optionally a description.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_JSON_MORE_DETAILS: Settings are named as the platform type names them, such as "script" for SSH, "hostname" for LDAP, "kerberos-realm" for Kerberos or "winrm-port" for WinRM: export a platform of that type to see them. Every platform is checked as when saved in the editor; if any is invalid, nothing is imported, and each invalid platform is listed with why.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_PASSWORDS: Exports never contain passwords, which never leave the server. A platform imported may give them among its settings, such as "winrm-admin-password" or "ldap-admin-password". A new platform that needs one is refused without it.
